title: The Shoreline of Knowing
statement: A map offers the confidence of record; gears model the stories we infer between its lines. Around them, the fish, fungi, bridge, and fragile witness mark what remains alive, displaced, or unknowable. The collage holds knowledge not as a boundary that closes, but as a shoreline where certainty gives way to speculation.
brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Represent the boundary between what you know, what you infer, and what you cannot know.

notes.note: Establishing a layered visual argument with cartography, mechanical diagrams, biological forms, architecture, and a historical bridge as distinct modes of knowing.

The source material makes the conceptual structure clear: the map can anchor knowable evidence, the gears can occupy the inferential middle, and the fungal, aquatic, and architectural forms can interrupt certainty with living or unreadable complexity.

notes.note: The current arrangement reads well as a layered field, but the unknowable zone needs a more visibly organic interruption and the inferential zone can use pattern rather than only machinery. I’m adding a small anemone fragment, textile fragment, and shell-text fragment as counterweights without disturbing the established map–bridge–figure structure.

After inspecting the completed canvas, the layered composition is balanced and legible: the bridge and map establish recorded knowledge, the fish and gears form an inferential center, and the fungi, anemones, shells, textile, and lightly drawn figure preserve an irreducible unknown. No further visual edits are needed.
